LEARNING PATH · CLASS 49 · ACTION WORDS · AGES 4–5

Action Words — twenty-four printable verb flashcards for kids.

Twenty-four printable action-word flashcards for ages four to five, in five shelves: the every-day shelf, the big-moves shelf, the make-and-do shelf, the go-and-play shelf and the people shelf. Every card shows four or five labeled actions a child can DO while naming them — bite the apple, run to the tree, mix the batter, wait your turn — and every card opens its own short page with one way to try it today. The first card of the deck leads, right here.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One card. Four or five actions. A body that is already doing them.

Verbs are the words you ACT OUT before you read them — and this class turns 118 of them into moves a body can rehearse. Every card prints a small cast of kids doing one thing each: the every-day cards walk a whole day from bite to bed, the big-moves cards run and jump and spin, the make-and-do cards build and stir and sort, the go-and-play cards ride and throw and win, and the people cards borrow and share and wait a turn. Say the word, do the move, and the verb sticks — because it was never a word to begin with. It was a thing your legs already knew.

One card a sitting is plenty. Start with the Every-Day Shelf — it opens with the deck’s own first card and the day you already live — then let the Big-Moves Shelf spend the wiggles, the Make & Do Shelf hand you the small jobs, the Go & Play Shelf take you outdoors and the People Shelf finish with the words that need a friend. Every card opens its own short page: the card itself, its labeled words quoted, one way to try it today, and a link back here.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the action words already live.

Sports, Movement & Play in Class 37 · Ages 4–5 ↗First Actions & Body Parts in Class 6 · Ages 9–12 months ↗Life Skills & Good Habits in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 37 runs the sports — and the Big-Moves Shelf here names the moves the warm-ups ride on: run, jump, kick, throw, catch. Class 6 was where the baby first stacked and pointed and waved; this class is where the big kid NAMES all of it. Class 32 builds the good habits — and the every-day and helping words here (clean, sweep, tie, pack) are the verbs those habits are made of. And when you want the next class, the Learning Path holds all forty-nine in order.

Say the word, do the move. Every card here works the moment a body joins in — pick one, act it out, and the verb is yours for keeps.

ACTION WORDS · CLASS 49 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 1 OF 24

Bite, Chew, Smell, Touch & Feel

Your body has five little workers and this card names each one: your teeth BITE and CHEW, your nose SMELLS, your fingers TOUCH, and your skin FEELS the softness of a towel. Five words, one you — every one of them already working before breakfast.

The card says

“BITE · CHEW · SMELL · TOUCH · FEEL” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Snack time is the drill: bite, chew, then sniff the snack before the second bite. Then a pet or a blanket for touch and feel — all five card words before the plate is empty.

Keep going

Eat, Drink, Sleep, Wake & Rest

This card is your day from sunrise to lights-out: EAT the breakfast, DRINK the milk, SLEEP the big night sleep, WAKE with a morning stretch, and REST when your body asks for a break. Your body runs on these five words — every single day.

The card says

“EAT · DRINK · SLEEP · WAKE · REST” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Tonight, say the card backwards at bedtime: rest done, wake coming, sleep next. In the morning, wake, eat, drink — the card is a day, and now you can read it.

This card is how friends talk: LOOK with your eyes, LISTEN with your ears, TALK with your words, SMILE to show you are glad, and LAUGH when something is truly funny. Two people and these five moves make a friendship.

Open, Close, Give, Take & Help

The kindest mechanics card: OPEN unboxes the surprise, CLOSE keeps the pieces together, GIVE hands the gift over, TAKE receives it with a thank-you, and HELP pulls a friend back onto their feet. Give and take make every playdate work.

The card says

“OPEN · CLOSE · GIVE · TAKE · HELP” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Wrap any small toy in paper and run the whole card: give the gift, watch it be taken, help close the paper again — then open it one more time. Bonus points for helping with the wrap-up.

ACTION WORDS · CLASS 49 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 6 OF 24

Tie, Untie, Fold, Carry & Hold

Careful hands, five jobs: TIE makes the lace or the scarf neat, UNTIE undoes the knot gently, FOLD turns paper into a card, CARRY holds the box steady on a walk, and HOLD keeps the book safe against your chest. These are the quiet-strong moves.

The card says

“TIE · UNTIE · FOLD · CARRY · HOLD” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Fold one piece of paper into a card for somebody, carry it to them without peeking, and hold it out with both hands. Tie the ribbon if there is one — untie it when they open it.

ACTION WORDS · CLASS 49 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 7 OF 24

Sit, Stand, Walk, Hop & Skip

From slowest to fastest, this card is your legs in order: SIT still for the story, STAND up tall, WALK one foot then the other, HOP on one leg like a flamingo, and SKIP with a little jump in every step. Five speeds, one kid, all of them yours.

The card says

“SIT · STAND · WALK · HOP · SKIP” — printed on the card.

Try it today

On any short walk, do the card in order: walk one block, hop five times, skip to the corner, stand tall at the door, then sit for the story. The whole deck in one trip.

Keep going

“RUN · JUMP · CLIMB · PUSH · PULL” — printed on the card.

Crawl, Kneel, Point, Clap & Wave

You did this card before you could even talk: CRAWL across the floor, KNEEL down to reach the low shelf, POINT at the thing you want, CLAP when you are proud, and WAVE bye-bye at the door. Now you get to name them.

“CRAWL · KNEEL · POINT · CLAP · WAVE” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Play the card game: your grown-up calls a word — crawl, kneel, point, clap, wave — and YOU do the move. Five calls, five moves, then swap so you get to be the caller.

ACTION WORDS · CLASS 49 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 19 OF 24

Win, Miss, Score, Kick & Hit

Game day has five words and you need them ALL: KICK sends the soccer ball, HIT swings the bat, SCORE lands the basket, WIN lifts the trophy — and MISS? Miss is what happens right before the next try. Every player on this card does all five, and that is the secret.

The card says

“WIN · MISS · SCORE · KICK · HIT” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Backyard three-try rule: kick three, hit three (with a grown-up pitching or a balloon), and count every miss out loud and proud — because on this card, a miss is just the word before the next try.

Keep going

Your voice is a dial with five settings, and this card names them all: SHOUT for across the playground, WHISPER for the secret, ASK when you wonder, ANSWER when someone wonders at you, and THINK before any of them come out. Loud, soft, curious, helpful, careful — all five are yours.

The card says

“SHOUT · WHISPER · ASK · ANSWER · THINK” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Play the five settings today: shout the countdown outside, whisper the next word, ask one real question, answer one, and think for three slow seconds before talking. The dial works best when you move it on purpose.

ACTION WORDS · CLASS 49 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 24 OF 24

Knock, Ring, Answer, Hang & Unhang

The politest card in the deck: KNOCK before you enter, RING the doorbell when your hands are full, ANSWER when the phone calls, HANG the receiver back when the talk is done, and UNHANG it when it is your turn to call. Doors and phones open for kids who know these words.

The card says

“KNOCK · RING · ANSWER · HANG · UNHANG” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Practise the door first: knock knock, wait, come in. Then a pretend phone call on a toy phone — dial, answer, talk, hang up, unhang and call grandma back.

Keep going
